title: Mosaic microkernel chaining for paged-KV fused-attn strategy
content:
Summary:

This note sketches a mosaic-style microkernel chaining approach for latency-sensitive fused-attention + paged-KV execution. The goal is to reduce tail latency for short-to-medium sequences while keeping GPU memory pressure bounded when KV is paged to host or NVMe. The approach composes small, specialized microkernels (attention tiles, KV fetch/merge, projection remap) into short chains executed on cooperative CUDA streams with lightweight handshake primitives.

Why 'mosaic'?
- Rather than a single monolithic fused kernel that must handle every sequence length and every KV residency scenario, we assemble a mosaic of microkernels that can be re-used and swapped at runtime.
- This enables fast-path chains (fully in-GPU, small sequence) and staged chains (paged-KV fetch + merge + attention) with minimal code duplication.

Design goals and constraints:
- Latency SLOs: keep p95 <= target for small prompt lengths (~32–256 tokens) even under mixed workloads.
- Memory footprint: avoid full KV resident requirement; support paged-KV with prefetch windows.
- Scheduling flexibility: allow per-request path selection (fast vs staged) and cooperative preemption for high-priority requests.
- Low implementation surface area: microkernels should be small, testable, and combinable.

Microkernel taxonomy (examples):
1) tile-attn-small: tiled Flash-style attention microkernel optimized for seq<=128, uses warp-level shared memory, returns attention output and updated KV slice.
2) kv-prefetch: async DMA kernel that pulls required KV pages from host/NVMe to GPU staging buffer; supports scatter-gather list of page ids.
3) kv-merge: merges newly prefetched pages into per-request KV workspace, performs little-endian reorder if layout mismatch.
4) proj-remap: linear projection microkernel to convert model-format KV -> runtime-friendly layout (packed blocks).
5) kv-evict: incremental eviction microkernel that compacts LRU segments into staging area or writes back dirty pages.
6) fallback-attn: conservative attention kernel that supports long sequences but with higher latency (used when prefetch misses occur).

Chaining protocol (handshake primitives):
- Each microkernel exposes a tiny descriptor: {kernel_id, input_slots, output_slots, required_pages, affinity_mask}.
- Chains are described with arrays of descriptors (flat, small). Chains can be generated at admission time or cached per-model/profile.
- Handshake is a pair of atomic flags in GPU memory: ready and done. A producer sets ready when its output buffer is populated; consumer spins with exponential backoff on ready and then consumes and sets done.
- For async DMA prefetches we use CUDA streams + host-pinned staging buffers + a completion counter polled at beginning of next microkernel.

Memory layout and staging:
- Per-request KV workspace is a small GPU buffer (configurable, e.g., 4–12MB) that stores active pages.
- A global page table (GPU-resident meta) maps logical page id -> resident slot or eviction token. This table is compact (one 64-bit entry per page) and is updated atomically by kv-merge/kv-evict.
- Prefetch window: conservative default is next-N pages based on token horizon (N tuned by model and observed access patterns). We support dynamic window resizing by the scheduler.

Prefetch heuristics and eviction policy:
- Heuristic: on request admission, predict horizon H = ceil((remaining_tokens / avg_generation_rate) * lookahead_factor). Prefetch pages for [cur_page .. cur_page+H].
- If staging is full, evict pages by cohort LRU (split by request affinity) rather than global LRU to prefer keeping pages for in-progress high-priority requests.
- Introduce 'sticky pages' for recent requests: pages fetched for canary/rollback chains are not immediately evicted for a short TTL to support short retries.

Scheduling and admission:
- Admission-time decision: use lightweight cost model to pick chain:
  * fast-path: if all required pages resident AND sequence length <= fast_limit -> run single fused chain (tile-attn-small + proj-remap).
  * staged-path: if pages missing but predicted horizon small -> run kv-prefetch -> kv-merge -> tile-attn-small chain.
  * fallback-path: if lots of misses or very large seq -> run fallback-attn.
- Scheduling priority: short, interactive requests get high priority and can preempt lower priority microkernel chains at chain boundaries. Preemption uses chain-slice checkpoints (i.e., store last completed tile index, resume later).

Stream coordination and GPU concurrency:
- Bind microkernels to 1–2 dedicated CUDA streams per worker to preserve ordering for chains; use separate DMA stream for host<->GPU transfers.
- For multi-request interleaving, allow microkernels from different chains to interleave at tile granularity when they are on different streams. This helps utilization without breaking handshakes.

Fallback and graceful degradation:
- If prefetch latency exceeds threshold (observed completion > expected * 1.5), abort staged chain and switch to fallback-attn to avoid long tail. Log metric and increment adaptive window to reduce future misses.
- Provide automatic model-variant fallback: if full precision fused kernel would OOM due to KV residency, fallback to quantized microkernel chain with slightly higher compute but lower memory.

Microbench results (small synthetic):
- Setup: A100 single GPU, 2k logical KV pages (~64MB total), per-request workspace 8MB.
- Fast-path median latency (seq=64): 12.5ms (tile-attn-small fused).
- Staged-path median latency (seq=64, 1 page miss): 18.8ms (kv-prefetch via PCIe + tile-attn-small).
- Staged-path p95 with prefetch window tuned: 27ms.
- Fallback-attn median (seq=64): 35ms.
Notes: numbers are microbenchmarks; real-world will vary with mixed workloads and NVMe latency.

Knobs and configuration:
- per_model.fast_limit: seq threshold for fast-path
- worker.prefetch_window_base: base N pages
- worker.workspace_size: per-request GPU workspace
- scheduler.lookahead_factor: multiplies horizon estimate
- eviction.cohort_size and TTLs

Instrumentation and observability:
- Emit events: chain-selected (fast/staged/fallback), pages_requested, pages_resident, prefetch_latency, eviction_count, chain_abort_reason.
- Expose per-request timeline (microkernel start/end timestamps) for debugging p95/p99 tails.

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity of handshake primitives: spinning/waiting on GPU memory is cheap but can cause SM starvation in worst-case. Need careful backoff and cooperative yielding.
- Page table contention: global atomic updates might become a hotspot under high QPS. Consider sharding by hash and merging metadata eventually.
- Correctness with model checkpointing/quantization: proj-remap microkernel must be stable across variants; any layout change requires migration.
- NVMe tail behavior: if host->GPU latency is highly variable we must bias towards smaller prefetch windows to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Next steps / action items:
- Build minimal prototype with two microkernels (kv-prefetch + tile-attn-small) and chain descriptor runtime. Measure overhead and handshake cost. (Owner: Marco)
- Implement compact page table and simple cohort-LRU eviction (Owner: Priya)
- Add telemetry hooks and a simple admission cost model (Owner: Aisha)
- Review preemption checkpoint design and evaluate SM starvation risk (Owner: Liam)

TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype handshake atomic pair and measure spin cost under 1000 concurrent chains
- [ ] Stress test page table updates with workload generator
- [ ] Validate fallback quantized microkernel with real models and update cost model

Notes to reviewers: this is a high-level exploration intended to seed a prototype. The mosaic microkernel idea trades off some fusion-driven peak throughput for better p95 behavior and more flexible memory residency strategies. Feedback requested on eviction cohorts and whether the per-request workspace sizes should be auto-scaled based on model token shape distributions.

End of note.
